ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every shareholder, corporate officer, legal representative, and beneficial owner (threshold ≥25%) against: (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list and French asset-freezing orders ('décisions de gel de fonds') issued under Articles L.562-1 to L.562-21 CMF; (iii) the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, required because the target payment rails include USD-clearing SWIFT LC and TT Wire transactions; (iv) the TRACFIN-aligned national PEP database implementing the 4th and 5th EU Anti-Money Laundering Directives; and (v) adverse-media and politically exposed person checks for any public-office-holding individual connected to the entity. Enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and a written AML opinion by a French avocat are required if any PEP, sanctions-list hit, or adverse-media flag is identified; all screening results must be archived for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by the Direction interministérielle du numérique, with prior name verification through the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) administered by INPI and supplementary RCS data extracts published through Infogreffe
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) may be composed in French, English, or another language provided it is expressed in Latin characters. If the underlying trade name originates in Chinese or another non-Latin script, it must be transliterated into Latin characters using standard pinyin or ISO 709:1982 international transliteration standards. The legal form 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' or the abbreviation 'SAS' and the registered-office city must be appended to the denomination on all corporate documents. The name must be lawful, distinctive, non-misleading, and not contrary to public order (ordre public) or good morals under Article L.224-1 of the Commercial Code; the proposed name must also be checked against trademarks registered with INPI and EUIPO to avoid identity or trademark infringement.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registrar (greffe) identifies the proposed name as identical or confusingly similar to an existing French legal entity or a protected sign, the incorporation formality is rejected through the Guichet unique electronic messaging center. The applicant may lodge an immediate administrative re-examination request with the juge commis à la surveillance du registre within ten days of the rejection notice, asserting priority, goodwill, or distinguishing features; within thirty days, a formal appeal may be filed under Article L.123-3 of the Commercial Code with the competent civil/commercial court for judicial review of the refusal. As a parallel remedy, the applicant should simultaneously file a substitute name application with a cover letter explaining the rationale for the rejected name. Any unreasonable refusal may be challenged before the Tribunal judiciaire.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible. An SAS may use an approved corporate domiciliation service (société de domiciliation) for its legal siège social, but the industrial scope — manufacture, aseptic tubing, and canning of ambient quick-cook tapioca pearls — requires a real, physically inspectionable production establishment. The pre-incorporation dossier must identify both the registered office and the actual production address to the Direction départementale de la protection des populations (DDPP) and the Direction générale de l'alimentation (DGAL). A purely virtual registered office without any administrative or industrial presence is non-compliant for this license-regulated food-manufacturing activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (estimated 70% to 85% probability within the first 12 months of obtaining the sanitary agrément), driven by unannounced hygiene inspections under EU Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and French national controls by DDPP/DGAL, plus labor-inspection and establishment-integrity checks by the Inspection du travail.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 to R.227-2 concerning the société par actions simplifiée; Articles L.123-1 et seq. concerning the Register of Commerce and Companies; Articles L.123-33 et seq. concerning mandatory electronic business formalities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent commercial registry is the Register of Commerce and Companies maintained by the competent commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce), with filings submitted through the national Guichet unique operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of incorporation of a legal entity submitted through the Guichet unique, supported by the executed SAS articles of association, beneficial-owner declaration, and required evidence of registered office and capital deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS; EUR 1 is legally sufficient, subject to adequate capitalization. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation and the balance must be paid within five years of registration. Cash contributions must be deposited with an authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations, which issues the capital-deposit certificate. The stated USD amount is an indicative conversion of the standard commercial-registry filing charge and excludes the variable legal-notice publication cost, beneficial-owner filing charge, translations, notarization, and professional fees.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept the subscription by the founding shareholder for the shares specified in the executed articles of association and acknowledge receipt of the applicable capital-deposit certificate. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [full French address], effective upon registration. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed President (Président) of the Company for an indefinite term, with the powers provided by law and the articles of association. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed Director-General (Directeur général), if applicable. Any officer is authorized to complete registration, banking, tax, employment, licensing, and publication formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate structure, name, and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique for business formalities; competent commercial registry for registration review
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select the SAS form, verify name availability through the INPI and commercial databases, determine the principal activity and registered office, and obtain written premises evidence. If the office is domiciled with a professional domiciliation provider, obtain the provider's authorization and contract. Ensure the proposed activity description accurately covers manufacture, packaging, storage, and wholesale of tapioca products.
required_dossiers: Executed domiciliation agreement, lease, or premises ownership evidence
Business activity description and principal establishment details
Identification documents for shareholders and officers
Foreign shareholder or officer corporate authority documents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the address, activity classification, or identity data through the Guichet unique before submission. Replace non-compliant premises evidence or provide a certified translation and legalization or apostille where requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the SAS articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private execution subject to filing with the INPI Guichet unique and review by the commercial registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles in French or with a reliable French translation. Include the corporate name, legal form, registered office, purpose, share capital, share classes, subscription and payment terms, governance powers, transfer restrictions, financial-year dates, and dissolution provisions. Execute the articles by all founders. A notarial deed is generally unnecessary unless real estate or another legally protected asset is contributed.
required_dossiers: Officer appointment decision or appointment clause
Power of attorney for filing agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Adopt corrected articles and re-execute all affected pages. Obtain a commissaire aux apports report where required for contributions in kind, unless a lawful exemption is used and documented.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit share capital and obtain the certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized French bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital account, provide the executed articles and identification of the company and contributors, transfer the subscribed cash capital, and obtain the certificate of deposit. The certificate must identify the company under formation and the deposited amount. The account is generally released or converted after registration and delivery of the Kbis extract.
required_dossiers: Corporate powers and legalized documents for corporate subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank know-your-customer requests, replace incomplete corporate documents, and use a notary or another authorized depositary if the bank declines onboarding. Do not file without evidence of the required cash deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Accredited French legal-notice publication service in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a notice of incorporation in an authorized journal or authorized online legal-notice medium. The notice must state the company name, form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, President, applicable transfer restrictions, and registration details required by the current publication rules. Obtain the certificate of publication for the registration file.
required_dossiers: Final articles or incorporation data sheet
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Republish a corrected notice where required and upload the replacement certificate. Ensure that the notice department matches the registered-office department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, routed to the competent commercial registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the electronic filing, select legal-form code SAS, complete beneficial-owner information, upload the signed articles and supporting documents, pay applicable charges, and electronically sign or authorize the submission. Upload documents in legible PDF format and provide certified French translations where required. Monitor the filing dashboard and preserve the filing receipt and tracking number.
required_dossiers: Officer declaration of non-conviction and parentage
Filing power of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer the registry's deficiency notice within the stated deadline through the Guichet unique, upload corrected or missing documents, and pay any additional charge. If rejected, cure the stated defect and resubmit; challenge a legally contestable registry decision before the competent court where appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration governance and tax onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent commercial registry, Service des impôts des entreprises, URSSAF, and the company's bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the Kbis extract, convert the temporary bank account into the operating account, record the share ledger and shareholder register, establish accounting records, confirm corporate tax and VAT registrations, and enroll for employer obligations before hiring. Adopt the first board or shareholder decisions required by the articles, including officer authority, bank mandates, accounting appointment, and licensing responsibility.
required_dossiers: Employer registration data, if employees will be hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct post-registration discrepancies with the registry or tax office, file amended beneficial-owner or establishment data, and suspend regulated operations until required tax, employment, and sector registrations are confirmed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The competent industrial and environmental authority is the prefect of the department, supported by the Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL). Food-hygiene matters are supervised by the Direction départementale de la protection des populations (DDPP), or the equivalent departmental authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Installation classée pour la protection de l'environnement (ICPE) declaration, registration, or environmental authorization, as applicable to the site's activity and capacity; food establishments must also complete the applicable food-business declaration under Regulation (EC) No. 852/2004. Products of non-animal origin generally do not require agrément sanitaire, but the final classification must be confirmed with the DDPP.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL), under the authority of the departmental prefect; the environmental-assessment opinion may involve the competent regional environmental authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Conditional. Tapioca processing and packaging may fall within ICPE nomenclature section 2220 or another applicable food-processing classification. The site may require declaration, registration, or authorization depending on process characteristics, storage quantities, energy use, waste streams, and daily production capacity. A full environmental assessment is required only where the applicable regulatory thresholds or case-by-case screening criteria are met.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Obtain any required wastewater discharge authorization and comply with applicable municipal sewer conditions, ICPE prescriptions, and the Order of 2 February 1998 where applicable. Control suspended solids, organic load, pH, temperature, and other parameters specified by the permit or sewer agreement. Control dust and VOC emissions from ingredients, heating, cleaning agents, and packaging; segregate and track hazardous and non-hazardous waste through authorized channels. Maintain spill prevention, sampling, monitoring, and waste-tracking records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before operation, obtain the required fire-safety review or approval from the competent fire and rescue service (Service départemental d'incendie et de secours, SDIS) where applicable, particularly for premises open to the public or subject to building and fire-safety controls. Complete electrical, machinery, pressure-equipment, ventilation, emergency-exit, and structural-load inspections required by the building permit, insurance, ICPE conditions, or occupational-safety rules. Comply with the French Labour Code through risk assessment, a documented DUERP, machine guarding, chemical-risk controls, occupational medical arrangements, training, emergency procedures, and workplace hygiene controls.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), acting through the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); business registration filings are made via the INPI Guichet unique (https://procedures.inpi.fr) and the tax portal is https://www.impots.gouv.fr. The customs administration (Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects - DGDDI) separately processes export clearance through DELTA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident entity with no French permanent establishment: appoint an accredited tax representative in France under Article 289 A CGI, then file the application for a French VAT number (TVA intracommunautaire) with the competent SIE; no SIREN is needed if the non-resident has no French establishment. For a French fixed establishment or a French SAS: register the entity with the INPI Guichet unique to obtain SIREN/SIRET and simultaneous INSEE codes, then the SIE allocates the French VAT number; the registration requires notarized corporate documents, identity proof for management, a power of attorney, and evidence of the appointed tax representative where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: SAS status is mandatorily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) at entity level; no check-the-box or general pass-through election exists. Available statutory elections include: group fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI for French companies under common 95% ownership; VAT group treatment for closely-linked persons under Article 1693 ter CGI; the option for tax consolidation of German/Italian subsidiaries via a French parent (Glaner/Jay-Pension); and the application of hybrid mismatch allocation rules under Articles 209, 212 bis, 212 bis A CGI with no elective hybrid default.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 for non-established foreign taxable persons: a foreign entity making its first taxable supply of goods or services in France must register for VAT before or at the time of that supply. The domestic small-business exemption (franchise en base de TVA) of EUR 85,000 for sales of goods and EUR 37,500 for services generally does not apply to non-EU-established businesses. An intra-Community distance-selling threshold of EUR 35,000 is only relevant for EU-established suppliers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France imposes mandatory e-invoicing on domestic B2B supplies and e-reporting of B2C transactions under the 2026-2027 reform. As of 1 September 2026 all companies must accept electronic invoices, and from 1 September 2027 all companies must issue e-invoices using the Factur-X or UBL 2.1 format. Invoices are cleared via the national Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or through accredited Partner Dematerialization Platforms (PDPs) connected via secure API; no digital stamp or real-time fiscal clearance by the tax authority is applied. Export declarations must be filed electronically through the DGDDI DELTA system using the SAD/DAU format.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies under Article 262(I)(1) CGI to supplies of tangible goods (including aseptic canned tapioca pearls) that are physically exported outside the EU by the supplier or by a third party on the supplier's behalf; the supplier must demonstrate that the goods were removed from French territory within the statutory time limits and that the specific goods were exported unaltered. For processing or offshore services connected to goods, 0% may apply when the customer belongs (établissement) outside the EU and the services directly relate to exported/imported goods; compliance with Article 259-D CGI (services related to goods) must be evidenced.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/DAU) with customs office exit confirmation via DELTA
Bill of Lading or other transport document (CMR, airway bill) evidencing physical exit from EU territory
Commercial invoice issued at 0% VAT with purpose of export
Packing list and product specification sheet for canned/tubed tapioca pearls
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer evidence showing receipt of export proceeds
Proof of direct transport/container tracking and warehouse/terminal handling records
Export licenses and processing/quality certificates required for food products (including sanitary certificates if requested by importing country)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The French tax administration may deny zero-rating where the export evidence is absent or contradictory; the export VAT exemption is then reversed and the standard 20% VAT is assessed on the invoice amount, together with late-payment interest (0.20% per month). Penalties range from 40% to 80% for negligence, bad-faith (mauvaise foi) or fraudulent concealment; in serious customs fraud cases, criminal penalties under the Code des Douanes may apply, including imprisonment of up to three years and fines of up to EUR 50,000, plus confiscation of goods and vehicles. The ordinary reassessment period is three years after the filing year, extended to ten years in cases of serious tax fraud or hidden tax activity.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank framework. Foreign-exchange activity is also governed by directly applicable European Union financial-services, AML, sanctions, payment-services, and market-infrastructure rules, together with French banking law administered by the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution and the Autorité des marchés financiers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and has full current-account convertibility. There is no general French exchange-control approval for receiving export proceeds, paying suppliers, repatriating profits, or converting euros into foreign currencies. Capital movements are generally unrestricted, subject to AML and counter-terrorist-financing controls, EU and French sanctions, beneficial-owner transparency, anti-market-abuse rules, payment-services requirements, and applicable foreign-direct-investment screening. A non-resident shareholder may generally fund the SAS by equity, shareholder loan, or other permitted financing without a foreign-exchange permit. Profit distributions require distributable profits, approved accounts, corporate approvals, solvency compliance, and appropriate withholding-tax analysis. French domestic withholding on dividends to non-residents may apply, subject to treaty relief, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, qualifying exemption conditions, beneficial-ownership requirements, anti-abuse rules, and required documentation. Banks may request corporate, tax, source-of-funds, and transaction-purpose evidence before releasing or converting funds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the Banque de France, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no general statutory deadline for converting foreign-currency export receipts into euros. Export proceeds may ordinarily be held in euro or foreign-currency accounts, subject to bank terms, accounting records, sanctions screening, tax compliance, customs documentation, and anti-money-laundering monitoring. Goods exports must be supported by appropriate customs and commercial documentation, including the relevant export declaration and evidence required for VAT treatment. Banks may impose operational deadlines or request proof of shipment, delivery, invoice settlement, and economic purpose; these are contractual or compliance requirements rather than a general French FX-surrender rule.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Deposit Account for SAS incorporation or capital increase; Operational Current Account; Foreign-Currency Collection Account; Trade-Finance Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional banking entity
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Deposit Account for SAS incorporation or capital increase; Operational Current Account; Foreign-Currency Collection Account; Commercial Letter of Credit and Documentary Collections Account
Capital Deposit Account for SAS incorporation or capital increase; Operational Current Account; Foreign-Currency Collection Account; Trade-Finance and FX-Hedging Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE group banking entities, including Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Epargne institutions
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Deposit Account where offered; Operational Current Account; Foreign-Currency Collection Account; Documentary Trade-Finance Account
Operational Current Account; Foreign-Currency Collection Account; limited or case-specific capital-deposit and trade-finance services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operational payments and collections, but low as a sole treasury bank for a manufacturing SAS requiring capital deposits, documentary letters of credit, extensive trade finance, cash-credit facilities, and sophisticated FX hedging. An electronic-money institution or payment institution established and licensed in France or another European Economic Area state may provide permitted services under PSD2 or the Electronic Money Directive, subject to authorization, passporting, safeguarding, AML controls, transaction limits, and product scope. A non-EEA offshore digital EMI cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services into France merely through an online interface unless it has an appropriate French or EEA authorization, passport, branch, or authorized agent arrangement. EMI safeguarded funds are not equivalent to deposits and generally do not provide the full bank deposit, credit, cash-management, documentary-credit, or capital-deposit functionality required by the SAS. The company should retain a regulated French or EEA bank as primary treasury institution and use a compliant fintech only as a documented secondary rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be available for a French SAS, particularly where the bank supports electronic identification and the company, directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners have verifiable EU or equivalent identity credentials. Banks may nevertheless require a physical meeting, certified identification, notarized or apostilled documents, live video identification, French address evidence, a local authorized signatory, or an in-person interview where ownership is non-resident, the structure is newly incorporated, the business is cross-border, the source of funds is complex, or the activity involves higher-risk jurisdictions. Capital-deposit accounts may be opened before incorporation, but release of the deposited capital normally requires evidence of registration and the company's current Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence. Bank policy, not a universal statutory rule, determines whether directors or beneficial owners must appear physically.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or layered ownership involving non-resident shareholders, nominee arrangements, trusts, bearer-like instruments, or inability to identify each ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles of association; shareholder register; ownership chart through every intermediate entity to natural-person ultimate beneficial owners; passports or national identity documents; residential-address evidence; tax-residence information; beneficial-owner declaration; corporate registry extracts; board or shareholder resolutions; explanation of commercial purpose and control rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SAS with no operating history, no French trading evidence, or projected transaction volumes inconsistent with the stated business model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed business plan; manufacturing and distribution contracts; supplier and customer list; projected monthly cash-flow schedule; expected currencies and countries; invoices or purchase orders; warehouse, production, or logistics arrangements; website and product documentation; management biographies; explanation of the tapioca-pearl manufacturing and export model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection or shareholder loan with unexplained source of funds, third-party remitter, circular funding, or high-value payment from a jurisdiction viewed as high risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder or lender funding agreement; board approval; bank statements showing accumulation of funds; audited financial statements; tax returns; sale-of-business or investment documents where relevant; remitter-to-shareholder relationship evidence; source-of-wealth memorandum; payment instruction identifying the SAS and transaction purpose; sanctions and adverse-media screening evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned parties, sanctioned countries, dual-use goods, opaque intermediaries, or counterparties inconsistent with the stated food-manufacturing activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty KYC files; beneficial-owner verification; sanctions-screening results; end-use and end-user statements; commercial contracts; product classification; customs documentation; shipping route; bills of lading; certificates of origin; supplier declarations; internal sanctions policy; escalation and approval records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cash activity, personal-account usage, unexplained cash deposits, or commingling of shareholder and company funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written prohibition on personal-account use; treasury policy; bank statements; cash-handling controls; payment-approval matrix; accounting ledger reconciliation; explanation of any historical exception; remediation evidence; forecast showing predominantly bank-to-bank commercial settlements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent company information across Kbis records, tax registrations, bank forms, websites, invoices, business codes, or beneficial-owner filings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent Kbis extract; INSEE/SIREN and SIRET evidence; VAT registration; signed articles; management-resolution package; corrected business description; explanation of industry classification; proof of registered office and operating premises; confirmation of authorized signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected cross-border receipts or payments routed through multiple countries without a clear economic rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-by-country transaction map; payment-flow diagram; intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing policy; invoices; shipping and customs evidence; treasury policy; explanation of collection-account and settlement-account functions; list of correspondent banks and payment service providers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, politically exposed person status, fraud indicators, insolvency history, or regulatory enforcement involving a director, shareholder, UBO, or key counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent identity verification; certified corporate records; legal explanation of historical matter; court or regulator disposition; compliance attestation; enhanced due-diligence questionnaire; source-of-wealth evidence; senior-management approval; ongoing-monitoring plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Requests for unsupported cash withdrawals, rapid pass-through transfers, unusual refunds, crypto-related flows, or transactions outside the approved food-manufacturing profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written transaction policy; approved payment matrix; invoice and contract support; refund rationale; counterparty verification; fraud-prevention controls; transaction-monitoring rules; management approval; periodic account-reconciliation reports; documented prohibition or controlled treatment of cryptocurrency-related funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity funding into the bank-designated SAS capital-deposit account before incorporation or before a registered capital increase. Use a regulated bank-to-bank transfer, preferably SWIFT MT103 with a unique end-to-end transaction reference and complete ordering-customer, beneficiary, and ultimate-funder information. Identify the beneficiary as the SAS or, for pre-incorporation capital, the company being formed through the applicable capital-deposit instructions. Use an explicit payment narrative such as 'share capital subscription' or 'capital increase contribution'; do not use generic personal transfers. Provide the subscription agreement, shareholder or board resolution, articles or draft articles, capital allocation, identity and beneficial-owner documents, source-of-funds evidence, remitter relationship, and bank-requested tax and AML information. Following registration or the capital increase, provide the Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence so the bank can release the funds to the operational account. For shareholder loans, use a separate written loan agreement, arm's-length terms, repayment schedule, transfer-pricing analysis where relevant, and a payment narrative identifying the loan. France does not generally use a universal FX purpose-code system for ordinary commercial wires; the bank's internal payment-purpose, compliance, and accounting classifications must nevertheless be completed accurately. Convert currencies through the bank or an authorized payment provider, retain exchange confirmations, and reconcile the receipt to the corporate ledger.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA framework, and SWIFT cross-border transfers, commonly using MT103 or its ISO 20022 successor, for non-SEPA or foreign-currency settlements. Include complete beneficiary, ordering-party, intermediary-bank, invoice, contract, currency, and payment-purpose information. For recurring suppliers, establish verified beneficiary controls, dual authorization, callback verification for bank-detail changes, sanctions screening, and three-way matching between purchase order, goods receipt, and invoice. For imports or higher-risk counterparties, use an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit confirmed where justified, issued through the French bank and advised through the beneficiary's bank. Define the Incoterm, presentation period, latest shipment date, required transport documents, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, insurance document, inspection certificate, and document-discrepancy rules. Alternative rails include documentary collections under URC 522, bank guarantees, and open-account payments supported by trade-credit insurance. Maintain customs declarations, import records, VAT evidence, shipping documents, and sanctions-screening records. A payment should not be released solely on a commercial invoice where the bank's documentary-credit, sanctions, fraud, or AML controls require additional evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts with an authorized bank for documented forecast or committed foreign-currency receipts and payments. The company should maintain a hedge policy, approved exposure limits, maturity matching, counterparty limits, confirmation records, and accounting treatment under the applicable French and European reporting framework.

Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity management, currency conversion, and maturity transformation, subject to bank documentation, appropriateness, counterparty credit limits, collateral or margin terms where applicable, and EMIR-related reporting or risk-mitigation requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with restricted convertibility or where physical delivery is unavailable, subject to product availability, bank eligibility, MiFID II conduct requirements, EMIR obligations, documentation of the underlying exposure, valuation and collateral provisions, and confirmation that the instrument is not being used for speculative activity.

Plain-vanilla currency options and option collars may be available for hedging identified commercial exposures, subject to suitability or appropriateness assessments, premium and break-cost analysis, bank documentation, board-approved risk limits, and clear disclosure of contingent obligations.

Cross-currency swaps may be used for longer-term shareholder loans, acquisition financing, or other genuine currency exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, EMIR requirements, collateral terms, valuation controls, and treasury committee approval.

Derivative transactions should be executed only with appropriately authorized EU or equivalent regulated counterparties. The SAS should document the underlying exposure, avoid unhedged leverage, monitor counterparty and liquidity risk, maintain daily or periodic valuation controls, and review whether the transaction qualifies for any applicable EMIR clearing, reporting, hedging, or risk-mitigation treatment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of result
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders or sole shareholder of the SAS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential court order to approve accounts, daily penalties, director liability, and regulatory enforcement; no automatic strike-off solely for late approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts and required accompanying documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry through the French one-stop business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval; two months where filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction, daily penalty payments, possible fine for the legal representative, and escalation toward administrative or judicial dissolution procedures in persistent cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and tax package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the financial year-end, or by the second business day following 1 May for a financial year ending on 31 December, subject to the applicable electronic filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty generally 10 percent of tax due, increased interest, and possible tax assessment or other penalties for material non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business tax compliance, including CFE assessment information where requested
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CFE is generally assessed annually; required declarations follow the applicable tax notice or electronic filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, penalties, and collection measures; CFE payment is separate from annual accounts filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French one-stop business formalities portal and competent Commercial Court Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No routine annual filing; update within 30 days after becoming aware of a change in beneficial ownership or related information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice, court-ordered compliance, fines for the legal representative, and possible restrictions affecting registration or access to business services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate information and statutory register review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records; documents made available to shareholders and auditors where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least annually before account approval and whenever a corporate event occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Invalid or defective corporate records may impair shareholder resolutions, expose officers to liability, and trigger disputes or regulatory sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SAS generally must appoint a statutory auditor when it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, or 50 average employees. Additional rules apply to qualifying groups and certain parent or subsidiary structures. A statutory auditor may also be required by court order or specific legal circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Commercial Code accounting rules and the French Accounting Standards Authority regulations under the French GAAP framework. IFRS may be used for consolidated accounts where legally permitted or required, but French GAAP generally governs the statutory individual accounts of an SAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require an annual standalone beneficial-owner confirmation for an SAS. The company must maintain accurate beneficial-owner information and file an update within 30 days of any change. The register should be reconciled annually against the cap table, shareholder agreements, voting rights, control arrangements, and director records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members or shareholder ownership records
Register of Directors and corporate officers
Minute book of shareholder and corporate decisions
Register of share transfers and movements, where applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 600-2,500 per year, depending on address, mail handling, domiciliation, and corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 4,000-15,000 per year for a non-complex SAS; higher for groups, regulated activities, inventory-intensive manufacturing, consolidation, or cross-border reporting

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax, plus a 3.3% social contribution on corporate income tax for companies meeting the statutory turnover and tax-liability thresholds, producing an effective marginal rate of approximately 25.83%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to ownership, turnover and paid-in-capital conditions. Certain qualifying patents and similar intellectual-property income may be taxed under the French intellectual-property regime at an effective 10% rate, subject to nexus and tracing requirements. The standard research tax credit is generally 30% of eligible research expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold, subject to statutory exclusions and documentation. Qualifying new businesses, innovation companies and businesses located in designated zones may receive conditional exemptions or reductions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited, subject to the annual utilization limitation of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. French tax losses may generally be carried back to the preceding financial year, subject to statutory limitations and an election.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the impots.gouv.fr professional account or by EDI-TDFC through an authorized intermediary. Supporting schedules normally include forms 2058-A-SD through 2058-F-SD, 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD, 2052-SD, 2053-SD and other applicable annexes.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; quarterly corporate income tax installments are generally payable on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with a final balance generally payable by the 15th day of the fourth month following the financial year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the annual return is generally due by the second business day after 1 May of the following year. For other year-ends, the return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. The tax balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end. Electronic filing and payment are mandatory for SAS entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, fiscal year dates, principal activity, tax office and filing capacity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French registered office or permanent-establishment details, the French SIREN number and the French tax service responsible for the entity. A non-resident shareholder is not entered as the French taxpayer unless it independently has a French taxable presence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065-SD taxable result and corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss, corporate income tax due, tax credits, foreign tax credits where applicable, instalments paid and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only profits attributable to the French SAS or French permanent establishment. Do not include foreign head-office profits unless French transfer-pricing, permanent-establishment or profit-allocation rules require an adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting profit or loss to taxable profit or loss, including non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, timing differences and tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document all permanent-establishment allocations, related-party adjustments, withholding taxes, non-deductible expenses and foreign-exchange items affecting the French tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-loss utilization, current-year loss determination and carryforward or carryback information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the French annual loss-utilization cap and maintain schedules supporting the origin, amount and remaining balance of losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit allocation and items affecting the tax calculation, including exempt or separately taxed income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Segregate ordinary French operating income from income subject to special regimes, foreign-source income and items excluded under an applicable tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions and relationships with related entities, including debt, royalties, services, guarantees, management charges and other controlled transactions where disclosure is required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all cross-border related-party transactions to the general ledger, intercompany agreements, customs data, invoices and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains, depreciation, provisions, fixed assets, shareholdings, reserves and other tax-basis information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French tax depreciation and capital-gain rules to French assets and maintain acquisition, disposal, valuation and ownership evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research tax credit, innovation tax credit, foreign tax credit and other applicable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits attributable to eligible French expenditure and retain technical, payroll, accounting and allocation evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax liquidation statement and payment of the final balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the final liability with installments, withholding credits and tax credits; payment must be made electronically from the relevant professional tax account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of non-deductible expenses and excluded charges, including certain luxury, excessive remuneration, penalties and non-business expenditure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude shareholder, group or foreign-head-office expenses lacking business purpose, arm's-length support or sufficient French nexus.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% for deliberate non-compliance and 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abusive concealment. Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules and relief provisions. Additional penalties may apply to inaccurate information, unjustified tax credits, failure to provide requested records and non-compliance with electronic filing or payment obligations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate income tax installment and balance payments through the impots.gouv.fr professional account, with payment references generated by the French tax administration.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly installments plus an annual final balance.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December. The fourth installment may be subject to a special percentage of estimated annual liability for larger companies. The final balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, tax period, payment type and amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the SAS SIREN and French corporate tax account; do not use the foreign parent company's tax identifier as the primary taxpayer reference.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount based on the prior year's corporate income tax or current-year estimate where permitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Base the payment on the French entity's expected French taxable profit, including documented transfer-pricing adjustments where relevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year corporate income tax less installments, credits and other permitted offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the balance to Form 2572-SD and the annual return before payment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment may trigger a 5% surcharge and 0.20% monthly late-payment interest. Underpayments caused by inaccurate returns may also trigger tax reassessment penalties of 10%, 40% or 80%, depending on the taxpayer's conduct.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The domestic French withholding tax rate on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders is generally 25%, subject to exemptions and tax-treaty reduction. Dividends paid by a French subsidiary to a qualifying EU parent may be exempt under the EU Parent-Subsidiary regime, generally requiring the minimum participation, holding-period, subject-to-tax and anti-abuse conditions. French resident individual shareholders are generally subject to a separate 12.8% income-tax withholding mechanism, plus social contributions, which is not the ordinary non-resident corporate rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner should provide a valid certificate of tax residence issued by its jurisdiction and complete the applicable French treaty forms, commonly Form 5000-SD and, for dividends, Form 5001-SD. Relief at source should be supported before payment where the payer and French tax administration procedures permit it. If full withholding was made, the non-resident generally files a refund claim with the French tax administration, supported by the certificate of residence, payment evidence, beneficial-ownership evidence, treaty entitlement and the withholding certificate. Anti-conduit, beneficial-owner, principal-purpose and anti-abuse rules must be satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax under ordinary domestic rules, subject to anti-abuse, special-regime and treaty provisions. Royalties and similar payments for the use of patents, know-how, trademarks, copyrights, software rights or equipment may generally be subject to a domestic French withholding rate of 25% when paid to a non-resident, subject to applicable treaty reduction or exemption. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive may eliminate withholding for qualifying associated companies meeting ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax and anti-abuse conditions. Treaty rates vary by source and recipient jurisdiction and must be verified under the applicable bilateral treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million. A French entity is generally subject to full transfer-pricing documentation obligations where its gross annual turnover or gross assets are at least EUR 400 million, or where it belongs to a group meeting the relevant statutory threshold, or where it is controlled by or controls an entity meeting the statutory conditions. The documentation consists principally of a Master File and Local File. Entities below the threshold remain subject to the arm's-length principle and may have simplified documentation and information obligations.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single general economic-substance regulation equivalent to a standalone offshore ESR statute. Substance is enforced through the arm's-length principle, permanent-establishment rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, general anti-abuse rules, abuse-of-law doctrine, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, hybrid-mismatch rules, principal-purpose testing under treaties and EU anti-avoidance measures. The SAS should maintain French operational substance proportionate to its manufacturing activity, including premises, personnel, production assets, decision-making, inventory control, quality systems, commercial risk and locally supported accounting records.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.documentation_and_reporting: Large taxpayers generally must maintain a Master File and Local File and may be required to file an annual transfer-pricing summary return. Country-by-country reporting applies to qualifying multinational groups meeting the EUR 750 million consolidated revenue threshold. Intercompany agreements, functional analyses, product-margin evidence, customs data, cost accounting and contemporaneous benchmarking should support all related-party transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.penalty_exposure: Failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation may trigger a penalty generally calculated by reference to the controlled transactions covered by the missing or incomplete documentation, subject to a statutory minimum, and may facilitate a profit adjustment. A reassessment may also be subject to a 40% or 80% penalty where deliberate or fraudulent conduct is established, together with late-payment interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of sales, false invoices, undeclared cash receipts, fabricated expenses, false transfer-pricing records, sham royalty or service charges, or deliberate VAT and corporate income tax underreporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, 40% penalty for deliberate non-compliance or 80% penalty for fraudulent maneuvers. Tax fraud may result in imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, with aggravated cases potentially reaching 7 years' imprisonment and EUR 3 million, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, civil liability for personal misconduct, contribution claims and tax-payment liability where they organize or knowingly participate in fraudulent conduct. Courts may impose professional prohibitions and confiscation. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may arise from judicial measures; imprisonment is possible after conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Accounting fraud and destruction of evidence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining false accounts, omitting mandatory accounting entries, backdating invoices, manipulating inventory or production costs, destroying records or obstructing a tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment and penalties, rejection of accounts, estimated assessment, criminal prosecution and possible imprisonment and fines under French commercial and criminal law. Obstruction or failure to provide records may produce additional administrative penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president, directors and de facto managers may face criminal prosecution, management bans, civil damages and personal tax-liability actions where their intentional or grossly negligent conduct caused non-payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially shifting manufacturing profit to a low-tax affiliate through unsupported royalties, management fees, procurement charges, financing costs, guarantees, inventory transfers or non-arm's-length product pricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment to the French taxable profit, denial of deductions, withholding-tax exposure, late-payment interest, documentation penalties and potential 40% or 80% fraud penalties where intentional manipulation is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed for deliberate misrepresentation, false records or participation in tax fraud; ordinary commercial exposure does not automatically pierce the SAS liability shield.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, sham substance or abusive treaty access
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal French SAS with no genuine premises, personnel, production capacity, decision-making or commercial risk to obtain treaty benefits, deduct financing costs or book artificial manufacturing profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, permanent-establishment findings, tax reassessment, withholding tax, abuse-of-law penalties and possible criminal fraud sanctions if deception is intentional.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable where they knowingly operate a sham structure, misstate beneficial ownership or use the company to conceal unlawful conduct. A shell-company label alone does not automatically create personal liability or criminality.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassification of tapioca products, false customs value or origin, import VAT evasion, carousel transactions, undeclared intra-EU movements, false export evidence or incorrect food-product documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of import duties and VAT, customs penalties, VAT fraud penalties, seizure or forfeiture of goods, suspension of customs facilities and criminal prosecution for serious fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may face criminal liability and civil claims for knowing participation. Customs and tax authorities may pursue personal liability in cases of fraud, asset dissipation or deliberate obstruction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, structuring transactions to avoid controls, concealing beneficial owners, processing suspicious cash or trade payments, or failing to identify counterparties and payment origin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transaction blocking, reporting to Tracfin where applicable, administrative sanctions, confiscation, criminal money-laundering penalties and imprisonment. Banks may terminate accounts or suspend payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly facilitate laundering may face criminal prosecution, imprisonment, fines, confiscation and professional bans. Travel restrictions may be ordered by judicial authorities but are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful profit repatriation and withholding-tax failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties or interest without applying required withholding, claiming treaty relief without beneficial ownership or residence evidence, or disguising distributions as deductible expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of withholding tax from the payer, interest, penalties, denial of deductions, treaty-benefit denial and potential shareholder-level reassessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SAS president and responsible officers may face civil liability for intentional or grossly negligent failure to withhold and remit tax; criminal liability requires proof of a qualifying offense or fraudulent conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manufacturing or importing ambient tapioca products without required food-safety registration, traceability, labeling, allergen controls, hygiene systems, product specifications or recall procedures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative injunctions, product withdrawal or recall, suspension or closure, fines and criminal penalties for unsafe or misleading products. Tax consequences may include denial of deductions and audit risk where records are unreliable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal or civil liability for knowingly placing unsafe or misleading food products on the market, particularly where injury, fraud or deliberate concealment is involved.
